_comment: THE SHELL↔APP CONFORMANCE MANIFEST (#905 Part 2). One row per first-party app, and the row is what every layer reads instead of hand-listing apps. Written because the coverage question 'why does photos get preference over the other mini apps' has no honest answer while each app's coverage is hand-authored: hand-writing a journey per app is O(apps) to author AND O(apps) to run, and app #9 arrives untested until someone remembers it. Making conformance a property of the manifest makes every app covered identically, and makes a NEW app covered the day it registers — or `bun run lint:app-conformance` fails the PR that registers it. Four tables in three trees have to agree for a tile tap to reach a screen: the registry (packages/design/src/apps.ts), the launcher catalog (apps/mobile/src/screens/home/catalog.ts), Home's navigate switch (apps/mobile/src/screens/Home.tsx), and the deep-link table (apps/mobile/src/deep-links.ts). Nothing linked them; each could move alone and stay green. This file is the fifth table that pins the other four, and the linter is what holds them against it. JSON rather than a TS module ON PURPOSE: the RNTL sweep imports it (resolveJsonModule), the linter reads it from plain node, and the Maestro layer's `.mjs` runners can read it without a build step — the one source of truth the layer allocation needs, readable from every layer that needs it.
